description: Design a simple 5-stage instruction pipeline (Fetch, Decode, Execute, Memory, Write Back) in Verilog. Each stage should be represented as a register that stores the current instruction at that stage. The pipeline should process a stream of instructions and handle basic control signals for instruction progression.

Create a Verilog module for a SPI master controller. The SPI master should be able to send and receive data with a SPI slave device. It should include parameters for clock polarity and phase, and control signals for chip select, clock, and data. The master should operate in a POL/PHASE configuration and handle input data to send to the slave as well as receiving data from the slave.
code:
module spi_master (
    input wire clk,          // System clock
    input wire reset,        // Asynchronous reset
    input wire start,        // Start transmission signal
    input wire [7:0] data_in, // Data to send to the slave
    output reg sclk,         // SPI clock output
    output reg mosi,         // Master Out Slave In
    input wire miso,         // Master In Slave Out
    output reg cs,           // Chip Select
    output reg [7:0] data_out, // Data received from the slave
    output reg done          // Transmission done signal
);
    parameter IDLE = 3'b000, SEND = 3'b001, RECEIVE = 3'b010, DONE = 3'b011;
    reg [2:0] state, next_state;
    reg [2:0] bit_counter;
    
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            sclk <= 0;
            cs <= 1;
            done <= 0;
            bit_counter <= 3'b000;
        end else begin
            state <= next_state;
        end
    end

    always @(*) begin
        next_state = state;
        case (state)
            IDLE: begin
                if (start) begin
                    next_state = SEND;
                    cs = 0; // Activate chip select
                end
            end
            SEND: begin
                if (bit_counter < 8) begin
                    sclk = ~sclk; // Toggle clock
                    if (sclk) begin
                        mosi = data_in[7 - bit_counter]; // Send bit
                    end
                    bit_counter = bit_counter + 1;
                end else begin
                    next_state = RECEIVE;
                    bit_counter = 0;
                end
            end
            RECEIVE: begin
                if (bit_counter < 8) begin
                    sclk = ~sclk;
                    if (!sclk) begin
                        data_out[7 - bit_counter] = miso; // Receive bit
                    end
                    bit_counter = bit_counter + 1;
                end else begin
                    next_state = DONE;
                end
            end
            DONE: begin
                cs = 1; // Deactivate chip select
                done = 1; // Indicate transmission done
                next_state = IDLE; // Return to idle
            end
        endcase
    end
endmodule

The output y should be rounded to the nearest integer (0 or 1).

Design a simple I2C controller module that can initiate a start condition, send a byte of data, and then initiate a stop condition. The controller should have the following inputs: `clk` (clock), `rst` (reset), `start` (to begin transmission), `data_in` (8-bit data to be sent), and outputs: `sda` (data line), `scl` (clock line), and `done` (indicates completion of transmission).
code:
module i2c_controller (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire start,
    input wire [7:0] data_in,
    output reg sda,
    output reg scl,
    output reg done
);
    reg [3:0] state;
    reg [7:0] data;
    reg [2:0] bit_count;

    localparam IDLE = 4'd0,
               START = 4'd1,
               SEND = 4'd2,
               STOP = 4'd3;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            sda <= 1;
            scl <= 1;
            done <= 0;
            bit_count <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start) begin
                        state <= START;
                        data <= data_in;
                        done <= 0;
                    end
                end
                START: begin
                    sda <= 0; // Start condition
                    state <= SEND;
                end
                SEND: begin
                    if (bit_count < 8) begin
                        sda <= data[7-bit_count]; // Send the data bit
                        scl <= 0; // Clock low
                        #1 scl <= 1; // Clock high
                        bit_count <= bit_count + 1;
                    end else begin
                        state <= STOP;
                    end
                end
                STOP: begin
                    sda <= 0; // Hold low during stop condition
                    scl <= 1; // Clock high
                    #1 sda <= 1; // Release SDA
                    done <= 1; // Transmission complete
                    state <= IDLE; // Go back to idle
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description:
Design a 4-bit shift register with parallel load capability. The shift register should have the following functionalities:
1. Shift left on the rising edge of the clock when the shift signal is high.
2. Shift right on the rising edge of the clock when the shift signal is low.
3. Load new data in parallel when the load signal is high, overriding the shift operations.
4. Maintain the current state when neither load nor shift signals are asserted.
code:
module shift_register (
    input wire clk,
    input wire load,
    input wire shift, 
    input wire [3:0] parallel_in,
    output reg [3:0] q
);
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (load) begin
            q <= parallel_in; // Load parallel input
        end else if (shift) begin
            q <= {q[2:0], 1'b0}; // Shift left
        end else if (!shift) begin
            q <= {1'b0, q[3:1]}; // Shift right
        end
        // else: Maintain current state
    end
endmodule

Create a Verilog module that implements a 2-bit Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM) encoder. The module should take a 2-bit input representing the in-phase (I) and quadrature (Q) components and produce a 4-bit output representing the QAM signal. The mapping is as follows:

01 -> 01
10 -> 10

description: Create a Verilog module that implements a simplified version of the SHA-256 hash function. The module should accept a 512-bit input message and produce a 256-bit output hash. The core operations of the SHA-256 algorithm, such as bitwise operations and modular additions, need to be simplified for this problem. Design an 8-bit serializer that takes an 8-bit parallel input and outputs a serial stream of bits. The serializer should serialize the input data bit by bit on the rising edge of a clock signal. The output should shift out the bits starting from the most significant bit (MSB) to the least significant bit (LSB). The serializer should also have a reset signal that initializes the output and the state of the serializer.
code:
module Serializer(
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [7:0] parallel_in,
    output reg serial_out
);
    reg [2:0] bit_counter;  // 3 bits to count from 0 to 7
    reg [7:0] shift_reg;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            serial_out <= 0;
            bit_counter <= 0;
            shift_reg <= 8'b0;
        end else begin
            if (bit_counter < 8) begin
                serial_out <= shift_reg[7];  // output the MSB
                shift_reg <= {shift_reg[6:0], 1'b0};  // shift left
                if (bit_counter == 0) begin
                    shift_reg <= parallel_in;  // load parallel input on first clock
                end
                bit_counter <= bit_counter + 1;
            end else begin
                serial_out <= 0;  // after 8 bits, output 0
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple branch predictor using a 2-bit saturating counter. The predictor should take a 2-bit input representing the current state of the branch (00: Strongly Not Taken, 01: Weakly Not Taken, 10: Weakly Taken, 11: Strongly Taken) and a single input representing the outcome of the branch (0 for Not Taken, 1 for Taken). Based on the outcome, the state should be updated accordingly.
code:
module branch_predictor (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [1:0] current_state,
    input outcome,
    output reg [1:0] next_state
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            next_state <= 2'b00; // Reset to Strongly Not Taken
        end else begin
            case (current_state)
                2'b00: next_state <= outcome ? 2'b01 : 2'b00; // Strongly Not Taken
                2'b01: next_state <= outcome ? 2'b10 : 2'b00; // Weakly Not Taken
                2'b10: next_state <= outcome ? 2'b11 : 2'b01; // Weakly Taken
                2'b11: next_state <= outcome ? 2'b11 : 2'b10; // Strongly Taken
                default: next_state <= 2'b00; // Default to Strongly Not Taken
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Cryptographically Secure Pseudo-Random Number Generator (CSPRNG) using a Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR) method. The generator should take a seed as input and produce a 5-bit output. The shift register should use taps at specific positions to create a pseudo-random sequence. Implement the seed loading, shifting, and output generation logic in Verilog.
code:
module CSPRNG (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [4:0] seed,
    output reg [4:0] random_out
);
    reg [4:0] lfsr;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            lfsr <= seed; // Load the seed
        end else begin
            // Shift and feedback calculation for a 5-bit LFSR with taps at positions 5 and 3
            lfsr <= {lfsr[3:0], lfsr[4] ^ lfsr[2]};
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        random_out <= lfsr; // Output the current state of LFSR
    end
endmodule

description:
Design a simple state machine with two states (S0 and S1). The state machine should toggle between these two states on the rising edge of a clock input. The state should be retained when the reset input is low. Implement the state machine with the following behavior:
- In state S0, if the input `data` is high, transition to state S1.
- In state S1, if the input `data` is low, transition to state S0.
code:
module state_machine (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire data,
    output reg state
);
    // State definitions
    parameter S0 = 1'b0;
    parameter S1 = 1'b1;

    // State register
    always @(posedge clk or negedge reset) begin
        if (!reset) begin
            state <= S0; // Reset to state S0
        end else begin
            case (state)
                S0: if (data) state <= S1; // Transition to S1
                S1: if (!data) state <= S0; // Transition to S0
                default: state <= S0; // Default case
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple UART transmitter module that takes a serial data input and outputs the transmitted data signal. The module should include parameters for baud rate and a clock input. The transmitter should shift the data out serially, starting from the least significant bit (LSB) to the most significant bit (MSB) along with a start bit and a stop bit.
code:
module uart_transmitter (
    input wire clk,             // Clock input
    input wire reset,           // Reset input
    input wire [7:0] data_in,   // 8-bit data input
    input wire transmit,        // Transmit enable signal
    output reg tx,             // Transmitted data output
    output reg busy            // Busy signal indicating transmission in progress
);
    reg [3:0] bit_counter;     // Counts the number of bits transmitted
    reg [9:0] shift_reg;       // Shift register for data transmission
    parameter BAUD_RATE = 9600; // Baud rate parameter

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            tx <= 1;              // Idle state for UART is high
            busy <= 0;
            bit_counter <= 0;
            shift_reg <= 10'b1111111111; // Default idle state
        end else if (transmit && !busy) begin
            busy <= 1;
            bit_counter <= 0;
            shift_reg <= {1'b1, data_in, 1'b0}; // Start bit + data + stop bit
        end else if (busy) begin
            tx <= shift_reg[bit_counter];
            bit_counter <= bit_counter + 1;
            if (bit_counter == 10) begin
                busy <= 0; // Transmission complete
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description:
Design a 24-bit ADC interface module that takes a 24-bit digital input and produces a 4-bit output based on the following logic:
- If the 24-bit input is less than 1/16 of the maximum value (i.e., less than 0x0FFFFFF / 16), output should be 0.
- If the 24-bit input is between 1/16 and 1/8 of the maximum value, output should be 1.
- If the 24-bit input is between 1/8 and 3/16 of the maximum value, output should be 2.
- If the 24-bit input is between 3/16 and 1/4 of the maximum value, output should be 3.
- If the 24-bit input is greater than or equal to 1/4 of the maximum value, output should be 4.
code:
module adc_interface (
    input [23:0] data_in,
    output reg [3:0] data_out
);
    always @(*) begin
        if (data_in < 24'h00FFFFF / 16) begin
            data_out = 4'b0000; // Output 0
        end else if (data_in < 24'h00FFFFF / 8) begin
            data_out = 4'b0001; // Output 1
        end else if (data_in < 24'h00FFFFF * 3 / 16) begin
            data_out = 4'b0010; // Output 2
        end else if (data_in < 24'h00FFFFF / 4) begin
            data_out = 4'b0011; // Output 3
        end else begin
            data_out = 4'b0100; // Output 4
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Create a 4-to-1 multiplexer that selects one of four input signals (I0, I1, I2, I3) based on a 2-bit select signal (S). The output is Y. The multiplexer should be implemented in Verilog, and the circuit should function correctly according to the select signal.

description: Design a simple Watchdog Timer in Verilog that resets after a specified timeout period unless a "kick" signal is received before the timeout. The timer should have a reset signal, a kick input, and an output that indicates a timeout (1 if timed out, 0 otherwise).

Design a simple PCIe interface receiver module in Verilog. The interface must handle incoming data packets and manage the acknowledgment signals. The module should have inputs for data, packet valid, and a clock signal. It should output an acknowledged signal when a packet is processed and a status signal indicating whether the packet is valid or not.
code:
module pcie_receiver (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire [31:0] data_in,
    input wire packet_valid,
    output reg ack,
    output reg status
);
    reg [31:0] packet_buffer;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            ack <= 0;
            status <= 0;
            packet_buffer <= 0;
        end else begin
            if (packet_valid) begin
                packet_buffer <= data_in;
                ack <= 1; // Acknowledge the packet
                status <= 1; // Indicate valid packet
            end else begin
                ack <= 0; // No acknowledgment
                status <= 0; // No valid packet
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a Direct Memory Access (DMA) controller that allows a peripheral device to transfer data to and from memory without involving the CPU. Design a simple OFDM transmitter that takes a stream of data bits and modulates them using QPSK (Quadrature Phase Shift Keying). The transmitter should have an input for a serial data stream, a clock input, and a reset input. The output should be a parallel data stream where each 2 bits are mapped to a QPSK symbol. The design should also include a state machine that controls the data processing.

Design a module that implements a simple Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS) controller. The controller receives a request signal (`req`), a target voltage (`target_voltage`), and a target frequency (`target_frequency`). When the request signal is asserted, the controller will gradually change the voltage and frequency to the target values. The voltage and frequency can change by one unit per clock cycle. The current voltage and frequency should be outputted as `current_voltage` and `current_frequency` respectively.
code:
module dvfs_controller (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire req,
    input wire [3:0] target_voltage, // 4-bit voltage
    input wire [3:0] target_frequency, // 4-bit frequency
    output reg [3:0] current_voltage,
    output reg [3:0] current_frequency
);
    
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            current_voltage <= 4'b0000; // Reset voltage
            current_frequency <= 4'b0000; // Reset frequency
        end else if (req) begin
            if (current_voltage < target_voltage) begin
                current_voltage <= current_voltage + 1;
            end else if (current_voltage > target_voltage) begin
                current_voltage <= current_voltage - 1;
            end
            
            if (current_frequency < target_frequency) begin
                current_frequency <= current_frequency + 1;
            end else if (current_frequency > target_frequency) begin
                current_frequency <= current_frequency - 1;
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: A Voltage-Controlled Oscillator (VCO) takes a control voltage as input and produces an output frequency that is proportional to the input voltage. Design a VCO module in Verilog that outputs a square wave with a frequency that varies based on a 4-bit control input. The frequency should have the following mapping: 0000 -> 1 Hz, 0001 -> 2 Hz, 0010 -> 4 Hz, ..., 1111 -> 16 Hz. Implement a counter that generates these frequencies based on a 100 Hz clock input.
code:
module vco (
    input clk,            // 100 Hz clock input
    input [3:0] ctrl,    // 4-bit control input
    output reg out       // Output square wave
);
    reg [6:0] count;      // 7-bit counter for frequency division
    reg [3:0] target;     // Target count based on control input

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        target <= (1 << ctrl); // Calculate target based on control input
        if (count >= target) begin
            out <= ~out;       // Toggle output when count reaches target
            count <= 0;       // Reset count
        end else begin
            count <= count + 1; // Increment count
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a simple DVFS (Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling) controller in Verilog that changes the frequency and voltage levels based on the input temperature sensor value. The controller should have a clock input, a reset input, a temperature input, and outputs for frequency and voltage levels. The frequency and voltage levels will be set based on predefined ranges of temperature values.
code:
module dvfs_controller(  
    input wire clk,  
    input wire reset,  
    input wire [7:0] temperature,  
    output reg [3:0] frequency,  // 4-bit frequency level  
    output reg [3:0] voltage     // 4-bit voltage level  
);  

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin  
        if (reset) begin  
            frequency <= 4'b0000;  
            voltage <= 4'b0000;  
        end else begin  
            case (temperature)  
                8'd0: begin  
                    frequency <= 4'b0001; // 1x frequency  
                    voltage <= 4'b0001;   // 1V  
                end

                    frequency <= 4'b0010; // 2x frequency  
                    voltage <= 4'b0010;   // 1.5V  
                end  
                8'd100: begin  
                    frequency <= 4'b0011; // 3x frequency  
                    voltage <= 4'b0011;   // 1.8V  
                end  
                8'd150: begin  
                    frequency <= 4'b0100; // 4x frequency  
                    voltage <= 4'b0100;   // 2V  
                end  
                8'd200: begin  
                    frequency <= 4'b0101; // 5x frequency  
                    voltage <= 4'b0101;   // 2.5V  
                end  
                default: begin  
                    frequency <= 4'b0000;  
                    voltage <= 4'b0000;  
                end  
            endcase  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

description: Design a JK flip-flop in Verilog that operates as follows: The flip-flop should toggle its output on each clock cycle when J and K inputs are both high. If J is high and K is low, the output should be set to high. If J is low and K is high, the output should be reset to low. If both J and K are low, the output should remain unchanged.
code:
module jk_flip_flop (
    input wire J,
    input wire K,
    input wire clk,
    output reg Q
);
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (J && K) begin
            Q <= ~Q; // Toggle
        end else if (J && !K) begin
            Q <= 1; // Set
        end else if (!J && K) begin
            Q <= 0; // Reset
        end
        // else Q remains unchanged
    end
endmodule

The input will be a 9-bit wide vector representing the intensity of each pixel in the 3x3 region, and the output will be an 8-bit value representing the edge magnitude.

module sobel_edge_detection(
    input [8:0] pixel_values, // 9-bit input for 3x3 pixels
    output reg [7:0] edge_magnitude // 8-bit output for edge magnitude
);
    wire signed [10:0] Gx, Gy; // Gradient in X and Y directions
    wire [7:0] abs_Gx, abs_Gy; // Absolute values of gradients

    // Sobel kernel for X direction
    assign Gx = 
        (pixel_values[8] + 2 * pixel_values[7] + pixel_values[6]) - // top row
        (pixel_values[2] + 2 * pixel_values[1] + pixel_values[0]);  // bottom row

    // Sobel kernel for Y direction
    assign Gy = 
        (pixel_values[6] + 2 * pixel_values[3] + pixel_values[0]) - // left column
        (pixel_values[8] + 2 * pixel_values[5] + pixel_values[2]);  // right column

    // Compute absolute values
    assign abs_Gx = (Gx < 0) ? -Gx[9:2] : Gx[9:2]; // right shift to keep in 8 bits
    assign abs_Gy = (Gy < 0) ? -Gy[9:2] : Gy[9:2]; // right shift to keep in 8 bits

    // Compute magnitude
    always @(*) begin
        edge_magnitude = abs_Gx + abs_Gy; // Simplified magnitude computation
    end

endmodule

The problem is to design an interrupt controller that handles multiple interrupt requests and provides an output signal indicating which interrupt has been accepted. The controller should prioritize interrupts such that irq[0] has the highest priority, followed by irq[1], and then irq[2]. When an interrupt is acknowledged, the controller should reset the active interrupt until another interrupt is received.
code:
module interrupt_controller(
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst_n,
    input wire [2:0] irq,
    input wire ack,
    output reg [2:0] int_out
);
    reg [2:0] irq_reg;

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            int_out <= 3'b000;
            irq_reg <= 3'b000;
        end else begin
            irq_reg <= irq;
            if (ack) begin
                int_out <= 3'b000; // Acknowledge resets the output
            end else begin
                if (irq_reg[0]) begin
                    int_out <= 3'b001; // irq[0] is active
                end else if (irq_reg[1]) begin
                    int_out <= 3'b010; // irq[1] is active
                end else if (irq_reg[2]) begin

description: Create a Verilog module that performs Cholesky decomposition on a 2x2 symmetric positive definite matrix. The input to the module will be a 4-bit wide matrix represented as two 4-bit inputs (a and b), and the output will be the lower triangular matrix elements (l11, l21, l22). The decomposition satisfies the equation A = L * L^T where A is the input matrix and L is the output lower triangular matrix.
code:
module CholeskyDecomp (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [3:0] a, // first row of matrix
    input [3:0] b, // second row of matrix
    output reg [3:0] l11,
    output reg [3:0] l21,
    output reg [3:0] l22
);

always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
    if (reset) begin
        l11 <= 0;
        l21 <= 0;
        l22 <= 0;
    end else begin
        // Cholesky decomposition calculations
        l11 <= a; // l11 is the first diagonal element
        l21 <= b / l11; // l21 is the second row first column element
        l22 <= b - (l21 * l21); // l22 is calculated from the second row second column
    end
end

endmodule

description: Design a simple RSA encryption module that takes 2 prime numbers, p and q, and a plaintext message as input. The module will compute the RSA public keys and encrypt the message. The RSA encryption is done using the formula: ciphertext = plaintext^e mod n, where n = p * q and e is a predefined public exponent (usually 65537). The outputs should be the public key (n, e) and the ciphertext.
code:
module rsa_encrypt (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [7:0] p, // First prime number (assumed to be provided in a suitable format)
    input wire [7:0] q, // Second prime number (assumed to be provided in a suitable format)
    input wire [7:0] plaintext, // Input plaintext message
    output reg [15:0] n, // n = p * q
    output reg [15:0] e, // Public exponent
    output reg [15:0] ciphertext // Encrypted message
);
    
    // Public exponent
    parameter public_exponent = 16'h0101; // 65537 in hexadecimal
    
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            n <= 0;
            e <= public_exponent;
            ciphertext <= 0;
        end else begin
            n <= p * q; // Calculate n
            ciphertext <= (plaintext ** public_exponent) % n; // Encrypt the message
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple SLAM-based system in Verilog that keeps track of a moving point in a 2D grid. The system will have a state that represents the current position of the point (x, y coordinates) and will update the position based on input direction (up, down, left, right) and a clock signal. The system should also have a reset signal to initialize the position to (0, 0).
code:
module SLAM(
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [1:0] direction, // 00: up, 01: down, 10: left, 11: right
    output reg [7:0] x,
    output reg [7:0] y
);

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            x <= 8'd0;
            y <= 8'd0;
        end else begin
            case (direction)
                2'b00: y <= y + 1; // move up
                2'b01: y <= y - 1; // move down
                2'b10: x <= x - 1; // move left
                2'b11: x <= x + 1; // move right
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a Master-Slave D-Latch using Verilog. The latch should have inputs for the data signal (D), the clock signal (CLK), and an output (Q). The output Q should follow the data input D when CLK is high (master phase) and hold the output when CLK is low (slave phase).

module master_slave_d_latch (
    input wire D,
    input wire CLK,
    output reg Q
);
    reg master_Q;

    always @(posedge CLK) begin
        master_Q <= D; // Capture D in master phase
    end

    always @(negedge CLK) begin
        Q <= master_Q; // Pass master_Q to Q in slave phase
    end
endmodule

endmodule

description: Design a TCP segmentation module that takes a 16-bit data input and a 1-bit control signal indicating whether to segment the data. description:
Design a convolutional encoder that takes a 2-bit input and generates a 4-bit output using the following generator polynomials:
- G1 = 101 (which corresponds to the first output bit)
- G2 = 111 (which corresponds to the second output bit)

The encoder should have a memory of one bit (i.e., it should have one historical bit to process the next input along with the current input). The state of this memory bit should be updated with each input. The output should be generated on each input clock cycle, and the system should be resettable.
code:
module convolutional_encoder (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [1:0] data_in,
    output reg [3:0] data_out
);
    reg memory;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            memory <= 1'b0;
            data_out <= 4'b0000;
        end else begin
            data_out[3] <= data_in[0] ^ memory; // first output from G1
            data_out[2] <= data_in[1] ^ memory; // second output from G2
            data_out[1] <= memory; // previous memory state
            data_out[0] <= data_in[0]; // current input (first bit)
            memory <= data_in[0]; // update memory with current input
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a SPI master controller that can send and receive data on the SPI bus. The controller should have the following specifications: it should have a 4-bit data input, a clock input, a chip select (CS) input, and a serial output (MOSI). Upon the assertion of the CS signal, the SPI master should transmit the 4-bit data on the rising edge of the clock signal. The SPI master should also be able to read 4 bits of data from the serial input (MISO) during the transmission. The data should be latched on the falling edge of the clock signal.
code:
module spi_master (
    input wire clk,
    input wire cs,
    input wire [3:0] data_in,
    input wire miso,
    output reg mosi,
    output reg [3:0] data_out
);
    reg [1:0] bit_cnt;
    
    always @(posedge clk or negedge cs) begin
        if (!cs) begin
            bit_cnt <= 0;
            data_out <= 0;
            mosi <= data_in[3]; // Start with the MSB
        end else if (bit_cnt < 4) begin
            mosi <= data_in[3 - bit_cnt]; // Send data
            bit_cnt <= bit_cnt + 1;
        end
    end

    always @(negedge clk) begin
        if (cs) begin
            data_out[3 - bit_cnt] <= miso; // Receive data
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a Verilog module that performs bilinear interpolation on four input pixel values (Q11, Q12, Q21, Q22) and provides an output pixel value (P) based on the fractional parts (x and y) for interpolation. The formula for bilinear interpolation is:  
P = (1 - x) * (1 - y) * Q11 + (1 - x) * y * Q12 + x * (1 - y) * Q21 + x * y * Q22  
where Q11, Q12, Q21, and Q22 are the input values, and x and y are the fractional parts in the range [0, 1].

    input [7:0] Q11, Q12, Q21, Q22,  // 8-bit pixel values
    input [7:0] x, y,                // 8-bit fractional parts (0-255)
    output reg [15:0] P               // 16-bit output pixel value
);
    always @* begin
        P = ( ( (255 - x) * (255 - y) * Q11 +
                  (255 - x) * y * Q12 +
                  x * (255 - y) * Q21 +
                  x * y * Q22 ) >> 16 ); // shifting to normalize output
    end
endmodule

Design a simple I2C (Inter-Integrated Circuit) controller in Verilog that can initiate a start condition, send a byte of data, and then generate a stop condition. The controller should have inputs for the clock (SCL), data line (SDA), and a start signal. It should also have outputs for the SDA line during transmission and a busy signal indicating that the controller is currently sending data.
code:
module I2C_Controller (
    input wire clk,            // System clock
    input wire start,          // Start condition signal
    input wire [7:0] data,     // Data to be sent
    output reg SDA,            // Data line
    output reg busy            // Busy indicator
);

    reg [3:0] state;           // State machine state
    reg [2:0] bit_count;       // Bit counter

    // State encoding
    localparam IDLE      = 4'b0000,
               START     = 4'b0001,
               SEND_DATA = 4'b0010,
               STOP      = 4'b0011;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        case (state)
            IDLE: begin
                busy <= 0;
                if (start) begin
                    state <= START;
                    busy <= 1;
                end
            end
            
            START: begin
                SDA <= 0; // Start condition
                state <= SEND_DATA;
            end
            
            SEND_DATA: begin
                if (bit_count < 8) begin
                    SDA <= data[7 - bit_count]; // Send MSB first
                    bit_count <= bit_count + 1;
                end else begin
                    state <= STOP;
                end
            end
            
            STOP: begin
                SDA <= 1; // Stop condition
                busy <= 0;
                state <= IDLE; // Go back to idle
                bit_count <= 0; // Reset bit count
            end
            
            default: state <= IDLE;
        endcase
    end
endmodule

Design a clock divider module in Verilog that takes an input clock and divides it by a specified factor. The output clock should toggle at a rate that is 1/factor of the input clock frequency. The module should also have an enable signal to allow or disallow the clock division.
code:
module clock_divider (
    input wire clk_in,      // Input clock
    input wire reset,       // Asynchronous reset
    input wire enable,      // Enable signal
    input wire [3:0] factor, // Division factor (1 to 15)
    output reg clk_out      // Output divided clock
);

    always @(posedge clk_in or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            count <= 0;
            clk_out <= 0;
        end else if (enable) begin
            if (count == (factor - 1)) begin
                clk_out <= ~clk_out; // Toggle output clock
                count <= 0; // Reset count
            end else begin
                count <= count + 1; // Increment count
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Kogge-Stone Adder in Verilog that takes two 5-bit binary numbers as inputs and produces a 6-bit output representing their sum. The adder should implement the Kogge-Stone prefix network to compute the carry bits and then use those carries to compute the sum bits.
code:
module KoggeStoneAdder (
    input [4:0] A,
    input [4:0] B,
    output [5:0] SUM
);
    wire [4:0] P; // Propagate
    wire [4:0] G; // Generate
    wire [4:0] C; // Carry

    assign P = A ^ B; // Propagate
    assign G = A & B; // Generate

    // Carry computation using Kogge-Stone
    assign C[0] = 0; // No carry-in
    assign C[1] = G[0]; // C1 = G0
    assign C[2] = G[1] | (P[1] & G[0]); // C2 = G1 + P1*G0
    assign C[3] = G[2] | (P[2] & G[1]) | (P[2] & P[1] & G[0]); // C3
    assign C[4] = G[3] | (P[3] & G[2]) | (P[3] & P[2] & G[1]) | (P[3] & P[2] & P[1] & G[0]); // C4

    // Sum computation
    assign SUM = {C[4], P[4] ^ C[4], P[3] ^ C[3], P[2] ^ C[2], P[1] ^ C[1], P[0] ^ C[0]};

endmodule

Design a simple I2C master controller in Verilog that can send a start condition, transmit a byte of data, and send a stop condition. The controller should have the following signals: `clk` (system clock), `start` (trigger to send start condition), `stop` (trigger to send stop condition), `data_in` (8-bit data input), `sda` (serial data line), and `scl` (serial clock line). The I2C protocol requires proper timing for the SDA and SCL signals during data transmission.
code:
module i2c_master (
    input clk,
    input start,
    input stop,
    input [7:0] data_in,
    output reg sda,
    output reg scl
);
    reg [3:0] state;
    reg [7:0] data_buffer;
    integer bit_index;

    parameter IDLE = 0;
    parameter START = 1;
    parameter TRANSFER = 2;
    parameter STOP = 3;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        case (state)
            IDLE: begin
                sda <= 1;  // Idle state SDA high
                scl <= 1;  // Idle state SCL high
                if (start) begin
                    state <= START;
                end
            end

            START: begin
                sda <= 0;  // Start condition
                state <= TRANSFER;
                data_buffer <= data_in; // Load data for transfer
                bit_index <= 0;
            end

            TRANSFER: begin
                scl <= 0;  // Prepare to send
                sda <= data_buffer[7 - bit_index]; // Send MSB first
                bit_index <= bit_index + 1;
                if (bit_index == 7) begin
                    state <= STOP; // Move to stop after sending all bits
                end
            end

            STOP: begin
                scl <= 1;  // Stop condition
                sda <= 1;  // SDA goes high after SCL
                state <= IDLE; // Go back to idle
            end

            default: state <= IDLE;
        endcase
    end
endmodule

Create a Verilog module that performs a linear regression calculation. The module should take in two data points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) as inputs and output the slope (m) and y-intercept (b) of the line that fits those two points using the formula:
m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1)
b = y1 - m * x1

    input [15:0] y1,
    input [15:0] x2,

description: Design a simple neural network layer that performs backpropagation for a single neuron.     input clk,                  // clock signal

    output reg [7:0] updated_weights // updated weights after backpropagation
);

    reg [7:0] error;

description: Design a simple Watchdog timer in Verilog that resets a counter every time an external signal (e.g., a "kick" signal) is received. If the "kick" signal is not received within a given timeout period, the timer should assert a reset signal. The timer should be parameterized to allow for different timeout values.
code:
module WatchdogTimer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset_n,
    input wire kick,
    output reg reset_signal
);
    parameter TIMEOUT = 10; // Timeout value in clock cycles
    reg [3:0] counter; // 4-bit counter to track time

    always @(posedge clk or negedge reset_n) begin
        if (!reset_n) begin
            counter <= 0;
            reset_signal <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (kick) begin
                counter <= 0; // Reset the counter on kick
                reset_signal <= 1'b0; // De-assert reset_signal
            end else if (counter < TIMEOUT) begin
                counter <= counter + 1; // Increment counter
                reset_signal <= 1'b0; // De-assert reset_signal
            end else begin
                reset_signal <= 1'b1; // Assert reset_signal if timeout
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

    input rst,
    input [3:0] request, // Request signals for each channel
    output reg [3:0] grant // Grant signal for the active channel

        if (rst) begin
            grant <= 4'b0000;
            current_channel <= 2'b00;

                grant <= 4'b0000; // Disable all grants
                grant[current_channel] <= 1; // Grant access to the current channel

When in the SEND state, it sends data; when in the RECEIVE state, it receives data. The controller should have a clock and a reset signal. module sata_controller (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire send_data,
    input wire receive_data,
    output reg [1:0] state // 00: IDLE, 01: SEND, 10: RECEIVE
);

    // State encoding
    parameter IDLE = 2'b00;
    parameter SEND = 2'b01;
    parameter RECEIVE = 2'b10;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (send_data) begin
                        state <= SEND;
                    end else if (receive_data) begin
                        state <= RECEIVE;
                    end
                end
                SEND: begin
                    state <= IDLE; // Return to IDLE after sending
                end
                RECEIVE: begin
                    state <= IDLE; // Return to IDLE after receiving
                end
                default: state <= IDLE;
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

            Q <= 0;

                2'b01: Q <= 0;         // Reset

    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [N*N-1:0] graph, // adjacency matrix
    output reg [N*N-1:0] dist // shortest path matrix
);
    integer i, j, k;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            dist <= graph;
        end else begin
            for (k = 0; k < N; k = k + 1) begin
                for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin
                    for (j = 0; j < N; j = j + 1) begin
                        if (dist[i*N+j] > dist[i*N+k] + dist[k*N+j]) begin
                            dist[i*N+j] <= dist[i*N+k] + dist[k*N+j];

                end

    end
endmodule

Create a LIFO stack module in Verilog that supports the following operations:
1. Push: Add a data element to the top of the stack.
2. Pop: Remove the top element from the stack and return it.
3. Peek: Return the top element without removing it.
4. isEmpty: Indicate if the stack is empty.
The stack should have a fixed size of 8 elements, and it should handle overflow and underflow conditions appropriately.
code:
module LIFO_Stack (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input push,
    input pop,
    input [7:0] data_in,
    output reg [7:0] data_out,
    output reg is_empty,
    output reg is_full
);
    reg [7:0] stack [0:7]; // 8 element stack
    reg [2:0] top; // points to the top of the stack

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            top <= 3'b111; // Set to -1 (no elements)
            is_empty <= 1'b1;
            is_full <= 1'b0;
            data_out <= 8'b0;
        end else begin
            if (push && !is_full) begin
                top <= top + 1;
                stack[top] <= data_in;
                is_empty <= 1'b0;
                if (top == 3'b111) is_full <= 1'b1; // Check if stack is full
            end
            
            if (pop && !is_empty) begin
                data_out <= stack[top];
                top <= top - 1;
                if (top == 3'b111) is_empty <= 1'b1; // Stack is empty now
                is_full <= 1'b0;
            end
            
            if (!pop) begin
                data_out <= stack[top]; // Peek operation
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a UART controller that can transmit data serially. The UART controller should take a parallel data input of 8 bits, a transmission enable signal, and a clock. Upon receiving the transmission enable, it should start sending the data bit by bit, with a start bit ('0') followed by the 8 data bits, and end with a stop bit ('1'). The controller should also have a ready signal that indicates when the UART is ready to take a new byte of data for transmission.
code:
module uart_controller (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire [7:0] data_in,
    input wire tx_enable,
    output reg tx,
    output reg ready
);

    reg [3:0] bit_count;
    reg [9:0] shift_reg; // 1 start bit + 8 data bits + 1 stop bit
    reg state;

    parameter IDLE = 1'b0;
    parameter TRANSMITTING = 1'b1;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            tx <= 1; // Idle state for UART is high
            ready <= 1;
            bit_count <= 0;
            state <= IDLE;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (tx_enable && ready) begin
                        shift_reg <= {1'b1, data_in, 1'b0}; // Prepare to send start bit + data + stop bit
                        bit_count <= 0;
                        tx <= 0; // Start bit
                        ready <= 0; // Not ready for new data
                        state <= TRANSMITTING;
                    end
                end
                TRANSMITTING: begin
                    if (bit_count < 10) begin
                        tx <= shift_reg[bit_count]; // Send one bit
                        bit_count <= bit_count + 1;
                    end else begin
                        tx <= 1; // Stop bit
                        ready <= 1; // Ready for new data
                        state <= IDLE;
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

The module should take an input signal and produce an output signal that is phase-locked to the input. You should include a frequency control word to adjust the output frequency, and a simple state machine to manage the PLL states.

module cfr_pll (
    input clk,             // System clock
    input rst,             // Reset signal
    input signal_in,       // Input signal for frequency recovery
    input [7:0] fctrl,     // Frequency control word
    output reg signal_out   // Output synchronized signal
);

    reg [1:0] state;      // State for the PLL
    parameter IDLE = 2'b00, LOCK = 2'b01, ADJUST = 2'b10;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            signal_out <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (signal_in) begin
                        state <= LOCK;
                    end
                end
                LOCK: begin
                    // Locking logic
                    signal_out <= signal_in; // Phase lock the input signal
                    state <= ADJUST; // Move to adjust state
                end
                ADJUST: begin
                    // Adjust output frequency based on control word
                    signal_out <= signal_in ^ fctrl[0]; // Simple frequency adjustment example
                    // Transition logic
                    if (fctrl == 8'h00) begin
                        state <= IDLE; // Go back to IDLE if control word is zero
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule
